description:
Conversion of existing terraced dwelling into three self-contained residential flats, comprising: Flat 1: 2-bedroom, 4-person unit (70.3 sqm) Flat 2: 1-bedroom, 2-person unit (57.2 sqm) Flat 3: Duplex 3-bedroom, 5-person unit (90.3 sqm)
with associated works: Part single-/part two-storey side and rear extensions, Loft extension via front and rear dormers,  Creation of front and rear lightwells, Provision of private/shared amenity space, secure cycle storage, and screened refuse/recycling facilities.
decision_conditions: The applicant has failed to provide any bicycle parking or show a location where it would be accessible and acceptable for all flats. The development would, therefore, be contrary to policies LP41 (Liveable Neighbourhoods), LP42 (Walking and Cycling), and LP43 (Transport and Development) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020) and policies T2 (Healthy streets), T4 (Assessing and mitigating transport impacts), and T5 (Cycling) of the London Plan (2021).

In the absence of a Unilateral Undertaking or a Section 106 Agreement securing appropriate mitigation by restricting future occupiers of the development from obtaining parking permits within the Controlled Parking Zone, the development would likely exacerbate existing parking stress and congestion on the surrounding highway network. The application is, therefore, contrary to policies LP43 (Transport and Development) and LP45 (Parking and Car-Free Development) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020), and policies&nbsp;T4 (Assessing and mitigating transport impacts) and T6 (Car parking)<br>of the London Plan (2021).

The applicant has failed to provide any refuse and recycling storage for the proposed development, thus failing to meet the requirements of policy LP57 (Waste) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020) and policy D6 (Housing quality and standards) of the London Plan (2021).

<p>﻿The application fails to provide adequate information to demonstrate how the proposed development would deliver a measurable Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) or be exempt from the requirements, contrary to the requirements set out in the Environment Act 2021. In the absence of this information, the local planning authority cannot determine the impact on local biodiversity or ensure compliance with policy LP47 (Biodiversity and Sites of Importance of Nature Conservation) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020), and policy G6 (Biodiversity and access to nature) of the London Plan (2021).&nbsp;</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of poor outlook and lack of sunlight/daylight, would provide a sub-standard form of accommodation for the occupiers of the basement flat (Flat 1). Furthermore, the provision of a family unit with no access to private external amenity space. As such, the proposal is contrary to policy D6 (Housing quality and standards) of the London Plan (2021), policies LP17 (Housing Design) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020), and the Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD (2009) and the GLA's&nbsp;<span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Technical Housing Standards- Nationally Described Space Standard </span>(2015).&nbsp;</p><p><span id="docs-internal-guid-b478d5a9-7fff-d239-4d41-add24706e982"></span><br></p>

In the absence of an Energy Statement, or&nbsp; Unilateral Undertaking or Section 106 Agreement securing a financial contribution towards carbon offsetting, the development fails to demonstrate how it meets policies LP54 (Overheating and Adapting to Climate Change) and LP55 (Mitigating Climate Change)&nbsp;of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020) and policies&nbsp;<span id="docs-internal-guid-41b70327-7fff-804e-4a41-5ab165241d1a">SI 2 (Minimising greenhouse gas emissions) and SI 4 (Managing heat risk) of the London Plan (2021).</span><div><span><br></span></div>

The applicant has failed to provide sufficient information in the form of a viability appraisal, nor agreed to enter a unilateral undertaking to contribute towards affordable housing in the borough, therefore failing to meet the requirements of policy LP13 (Affordable Housing) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020), and Hackney's&nbsp;<span id="docs-internal-guid-1dc14676-7fff-bc15-04b2-34f246eee49a"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Planning Contributions SPD (2020).</span></span>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-351feef4-7fff-e9d1-11a4-10dec0cd9bae"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Due to insufficient information, the proposal fails to demonstrate how Part C of policy LP22 (Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO)) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020) is met, which resists the</span></span> loss of good quality HMO properties unless adequate replacement facilities are provided, or it can be demonstrated that the existing facility is no longer required. </p>

The size and bulk of the proposed ground-floor rear extension, at 3.5m tall, and south of the attached neighbour, would harm the amenities of the occupiers of No.44 Bayston Road through a loss of daylight and sunlight, and it would have an overbearing impact. As such, the proposal fails to comply with policy LP2 (Development and Amenity) of the Hackney Local Plan (2020), policy D6 (Housing quality and standards) of the London Plan (2021), and Hackney's Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD (2009).
